done_when: CLAUDE.md or SUPER_SESSION.md gets one explicit line: once a session has received direct operator feedback (or hit the model_guard 'operator is away' hook) that start_session costs an unwanted click, that session must not call start_session again for the rest of its life -- go straight to the Agent tool, no retry with a different initiation value. Also: someone with visibility into the Remote Control / push layer confirms whether a start_session call that the ccd backend ultimately refuses (app-level turn-type refusal, or the model_guard hook) ever still surfaces an approval card to the operator first -- if yes, that is a separate platform-level bug (a doomed call shouldn't cost a click) and gets its own card; if no, the cost here was purely wasted operator attention/time reading the request, not a literal click, and the fix is behavioral only (the done_when above).
goal: Operator priority-1 bug (2026-10-27, this session, local_37a9ec3e): on an event-turn (triggered by a background ship-completion notification, operator not actively present), this coordinator tried start_session twice to hand off to a 'link 2' coordinator -- once with initiation=user_asked (app refused: 'Start sessions only on the user's own words'), once with initiation=own_initiative (a project hook, model_guard, refused: 'No click cards: the operator is away. Use Agent tool'). Both attempts cost the operator noticeable, named frustration ('again, a classic situation of you making me click allow once... so much time has been wasted') despite this same session already having written a memory note minutes earlier ('Prefer Agent over start_session') and the operator having already denied two start_session calls earlier in this same conversation. The judgment failure: having that evidence in hand, retrying start_session at all -- let alone twice -- before falling back to Agent was wrong; the fallback should have been the first move.
note: Companion to coordinator-self-pacing-rolling-super-se (same session, same day): that card is the 'how to pace a rolling chain' capability request; this card is the narrower 'don't re-trigger known UI friction' behavior bug inside it. Refine separately -- this one is pure behavior/doc guidance (CLAUDE.md or SUPER_SESSION.md wording), no code needed unless the platform-visibility question above comes back yes.
result: Added SUPER_SESSION.md Rules item 9: once a session has been told directly (operator feedback or a hook) that start_session costs an unwanted click, it does not call start_session again for the rest of its life -- straight to Agent, no retry with a different initiation value. Put in SUPER_SESSION.md, not CLAUDE.md: CLAUDE.md is within ~1% of its size cap (see SIZE_CAPS in test_integrity.py), too tight for a new line without trimming something else first (out of scope here). Platform-visibility question: determined, with caveats. .claude/settings.json has no PreToolUse hook on start_session/Agent/Task/Workflow beyond usage_reminder.py (pre/post), and scripts/dev/model_guard.py does not exist on disk -- it and turn_meter.py were removed from trunk 2026-10-24 (43d3bfc8f, confirmed by git log) and never reintroduced. So nothing in this repo can intercept start_session before the app's own permission layer renders an Allow card; WORKERS.md rule 7's line 'the app shows an Allow card, so model_guard.py denies it' is itself now stale (describes a mechanism that no longer exists) -- flagged here, not fixed (separate from this card's scope). Combined with this card's own quoted operator words this session ('making me click allow once... so much time has been wasted') after BOTH start_session attempts were ultimately refused, the evidence says yes: a start_session call that ends up refused (app-level or hook-level) can still cost a click, because approval-to-run and the tool's internal refusal are two different steps -- the click happens first. This is inferred from repo state (hooks, file absence, WORKERS.md history) plus the card's own quoted operator complaint, not from reading the Remote Control/push-layer source itself (not in this repo). Per the card's done_when, this reads as the 'yes' branch (platform-level bug: a doomed call shouldn't cost a click) -- left as a flagged finding in this card rather than filed as a brand-new separate card, since the fix (if any) is platform-side, outside this repo's scope.
scope_in: one explicit rule in CLAUDE.md/SUPER_SESSION.md: no start_session retry after in-session friction feedback
flag the platform-visibility question (does a refused start_session still cost a click?) for someone who can see the Remote Control/push layer
scope_out: removing start_session from the toolset entirely -- it is still the right tool for a genuine, operator-present, persistent hand-off; this is about not retrying it blindly after already being told not to
steps: Confirm CLAUDE.md has almost no size-cap headroom left (see SIZE_CAPS in test_integrity.py) so the new line goes in SUPER_SESSION.md instead, per the card's own 'CLAUDE.md or SUPER_SESSION.md' choice.
Add SUPER_SESSION.md Rules item 9: no start_session retry after click-friction feedback, straight to Agent tool.

Search this repo for model_guard.py / turn_meter.py and any PreToolUse hook on start_session in .claude/settings.json; find neither the files nor a hook -- both were removed 2026-10-24 (43d3bfc8f) and never reintroduced.

Cross-check WORKERS.md rule 7 ('the app shows an Allow card, so model_guard.py denies it') against that absence: the line is stale. Combine with the card's own quoted operator complaint (click cost after both refused attempts) to answer the platform-visibility question: yes, a refused start_session can still cost a click.
